rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Register match.

Adding rules is only half of it; subtracting the dead ones is the other half.', L35), peer-warm push-back language ('Push back where Claude generalises', L28). Flinch-greps ('just a simple', 'trust the agent', leash/niceness metaphors) -> zero hits. No atmospheric imagery (no darkness/body-state/cosmic metaphors) to mis-fire in any voice. No '**Remember**/Hold onto/Keep in mind/Never forget' wrapper -> zero hits. No metaphor-keyword valence collision (no cargo/theatre/ritual/tourist/poster noun used). No negation-callout ('we don't X'/'we refuse') present to self-contradict. Mood-arc: file's stated target is 'practitioner fluency' (L67), matching AE101's learning-through-contrast/practitioner-fluency arc position, not the forward-launch beat that would require Risto-lead — consistent, since this file is Beat 1 of M6 (L65), not the arc close.

No creator name ('Antti'/'the creator'/'the author') in body -- grep -inE 'Antti|the creator|the author' scoped to 1-47 -> zero. No author-'we' -- greps.author_we body_hits 0, CLEAN. Timing: '**Time:** 20 minutes.' sits at line 3, directly below the H1, total-only, no phase breakdown -- correct for an ATOMIC exercise (maintainer L50: 'Atomic — no phase markers'), so line 3 is legitimately hand-authored per the rule's own atomic-exception clause. No belief-name/number reference, no lecture-authorial-meta to check (this is an exercise, not a lecture).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Watch out for planting jargon too early.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Audit closer when trimming body-prose forcing function.

(L30); 'Push back if the diff touches more than the one rule you flagged... One rule cut, no more.' (L44). No 'that one'/'this answer'/'with it in front of you' vague-referent closers found on a cold read.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: The `**What happened:**` block is OPTIONAL — default is to omit it (Antti-directed 2026-08-12, mandation removed from `curriculum/exercises/README.md`).
rules_evaluated.evidence: L46: '**What happened:** A one-screen gap map across memory / verifier / skill and one stale rule cut in place.' Moves 1 (count+noun: 'a one-screen gap map... and one stale rule cut') and the noun-phrase-not-verb-narrated shape are clean, and the grep tell (^\*\*What happened:\*\* You) does not fire. But move 3 ('land on the destination — where it now lives or what reads it next') is weak: 'in place' repeats the EDIT MECHANIC (confirmed by the maintainer's own gloss at L44: '"In place" is loose wording'), not a forward-pointing destination the way the exemplars do ('living in your personal skills folder. Shipped.', 'settled on disk'). The block passes on two of three moves; the third recycles a word already spent on describing the mechanic rather than pointing at where the edited CLAUDE.local.md now stands.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Land move 3 on the artifact's ongoing state, e.g. '...and one stale rule cut from CLAUDE.local.md, one rule lighter going into M7.' rather than repeating 'in place'.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No combative verbs about the agent in body prose.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Headers must be literally true about the mechanism.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All four H2s describe exactly what their section does: 'Diff the two sessions, rank the gaps' (diffing + ranking both happen there), 'Read the contrast, push back where it generalises', 'Cut one stale rule the diagnosis killed', 'Say go, unless the cut spreads past the one rule'. No spatial-metaphor mismatch, no 'other X' with no named primary.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Machine-cadence fat — the shape of good prose without the content.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No empty negation ('X, not Y' with an unguessable Y), no deictic drumroll ('That is the X.'), no bold-label echo, no citation/appendix duplication in body. 'no fork' (L7) is a genuine disambiguation (worktree vs. fork are both plausible reads), not an empty negation.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't state a count the adjacent list already holds.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 'three to five items' (L30) and 'two sessions' (L9, L13) are not restating a count the reader can already see in an adjacent visible list -- they are targets for output the student has not yet produced (via Claude), the case the rule doesn't govern. No numeral sits directly above/below a bulleted enumeration of the same items in this file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A slogan that is false as stated is not punchy framing — run the truth test before reaching for §12.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L13: '**The point:** two sessions are enough to place every lesson.' Reads as an unqualified sufficiency claim ('enough... every lesson'), not scoped to an artifact/corpus/dated finding. The rule's own cheapest-counterexample heuristic ('the curriculum's own contingency plan') finds a counterexample inside THIS SAME FILE: the Failure modes block (L75-77) documents three concrete ways two sessions do NOT place the lesson on their own — Generalised diff, Packaging over-credit, Rule-cut dodge — i.e. the diagnostic PROCESS (rank, push back, quote) is what does the work, not merely holding two sessions. As literally stated the slogan has no true reading; a hedge would make it worse per the rule's guidance.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Either scope the line to what the exercise actually claims ('Two sessions, read hard, are enough to place every lesson' or 'Two sessions give you what you need to place every lesson — if you push for the quote') or drop 'every' and let the Failure modes section stand as the honest boundary.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Say it once, at its most concrete, then at most one sentence that generalises it. Style, not a gate.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 'Rules-files have a half-life. Adding rules is only half of it; subtracting the dead ones is the other half.' (L35) is a concrete claim + one generalising sentence, then stops -- no third sentence. Checked whether §21 owns 'The point: two sessions are enough to place every lesson' (L13) before filing here per the rule's own instruction ('Check whether §21 owns the sentence before filing here') -- it does (filed above), so this rule doesn't separately fire on it. No prose restates what an adjacent prompt or header already says (each body lead-in stays a compressed skim-cue per check_prompts §2, not a full restatement).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Aspirational destination, never corrective gap.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No corrective-gap framing ('you already think you're using X', 'you're missing Y'). No ability-tier phrasing ('at your scale', 'for a beginner', 'a senior would already know'). No identity-split criterion (tourist/practitioner) present. The one pre-flight decision in body -- 'M5's session may still be running the re-send; ... decide whether it is done enough, should be stopped, or counts as the partial artefact.' (L7) -- is a genuinely plausibly-failable variable (M5's session state is unknown going in), not a rote environment check.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Earn every technical term on first use.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 'worktree' and branch-naming are audience-assumed-known (AE101 engineer audience, per §2's carve-out). 'packaging'/'un-packaged'/'the re-send' presuppose M4/M5 artefacts the body explicitly says the student already holds (L19-20) rather than introducing them cold.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Memory vs context — use deliberately.
rules_evaluated.evidence: 'memory' is used correctly at L46 ('across memory / verifier / skill') referring to the persistent CLAUDE.local.md rules-file, never conflated with ambient runtime 'context'. 'context' does not appear in body at all.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Golden path only in body — THIS RULE HAS AN EXCEPTION; read to the boundary before cutting anything.

The one conditional in body ('If it asks, just say go.', L43) handles an expected, normal agent behaviour (a pause before a config-file edit) with a one-line rescue, which is the time-critical/non-obvious-rescue case the boundary clause keeps in body -- not a generic FAQ branch.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Trust Claude's defaults for structure.

P2 uses a post-action report ('Show me the line you cut...') rather than a pre-save confirm, consistent with the surrounding prompt design; neither prompt appends a cosmetic formatting spec.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Q1/Q2/Q3 retro interview is banned at every module. Compound-shape varies per module — never repeat same Debrief.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: LLM-vs-agent-vs-Claude vocabulary discipline.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body's word choice runs 'Claude' x7 (L22, L28 x1, L29 x2, L37, L43, L44) against 'agent' x0 outside a quoted example (the one 'agent' hit at L29 is inside a quoted bad-example Claude might write, not the file's own descriptive choice) -- close to the exact ratio pattern the rule itself flags as a diagnostic tell ('body Claude-count >> agent-count (e.g., 10:0) = assistant-shaped framing'). Two uses are clean addressee grammar ('Ask Claude to...', L22, L37). But at least two read as describing the agent's own autonomous behaviour during a delegated task rather than addressing it -- L28 'Claude will likely open with a four-dimension plan summary...' and L43 'Claude may pause before editing ./CLAUDE.local.md' both describe execution/behavioural tendencies (active stance), which the rule's default routes to 'the agent'. Genuinely arguable given the paragraph maintains referential continuity with the addressee named two sentences earlier -- flagging for a maintainer call rather than asserting a clean violation.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Consider 'the agent will likely open with...' (L28) and 'the agent may pause before editing ./CLAUDE.local.md' (L43) to match the acting/agent default, or confirm the addressee-continuity reading is the intended house style.

rules_evaluated.evidence: 'drift' (L22) is used correctly, pulled straight from the training's own theory-spine vocabulary (explicitly listed in the rule as a house term) rather than an invented synonym.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Name the artifact, not the act.

The act-verb 'say' narrates the physical utterance of a filler continuation word ('go'), which is the same shape the rule explicitly bans by name -- its own example list includes 'saying continue' as banned. 'go' here functions identically to the rule's own filler-case exemplar ('continue, go on -- where the prompt-noun costs nothing'), and is not the load-bearing-trigger-string carve-out (no fence in this file is waiting on the literal word 'go').
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Recast as an artifact: e.g. 'If it asks, a quick "go" is enough.'

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: The curriculum does not narrate itself — subject test, then deletion test.

No arc-positioning sentence found to delete-test.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Mood is a design constraint, not a garnish.

Not a sustained-doubt module, so the verification-step ban doesn't apply.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Exercise headers pass the build-squint test.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Reading only the four H2s cold ('Diff the two sessions, rank the gaps' -> 'Read the contrast, push back where it generalises' -> 'Cut one stale rule the diagnosis killed' -> 'Say go, unless the cut spreads past the one rule') reconstructs the exercise's build (a ranked gap map, then a scoped rule cut) without reading the body. H1 'Map the gaps, cut the rule' names the deliverable, not a technique.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No placeholders inside fences.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Read both registry files (curriculum/prompts/spot-gaps-build-the-loop-1.md, -2.md) in full -- no [BRACKETS]-style placeholder in either fence body; both are fully concrete, self-contained prompt text.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every prompt block: one-sentence action lead-in.
rules_evaluated.evidence: P1's lead-in (L22, 'Ask Claude to read both sessions side by side and name where packaging caught, where it missed, and what new shapes of drift it introduced.') is 25 words (echo -n ... | wc -w -> 25) and, per §2a's own bloat tell, enumerates three of the fence's four named dimensions almost verbatim ('what packaging caught' / 'where it missed' mirror the fence's own bullet leads 'What packaging caught:' / 'What packaging missed:'), leaving only 'where the fix belongs' unmirrored. This is the exact shape §2a names as the failure ('the lead-in enumerates the prompt's clauses'). P2's lead-in (L37) is a clean goal-summary, not a clause enumeration -- fine as is.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Mirror only the fence's opening move per §38 (e.g. 'Ask Claude to read both sessions and walk the diff across four dimensions.') and let the fence carry the specific caught/missed/introduced/fix-belongs breakdown.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Canonical shape — lead-in, label with destination, blank line, fence.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Both prompts follow lead-in / blank / '**Prompt** *(Claude Code)*' [P2: with context suffix] / blank / fence exactly (confirmed against the expanded view). No 'copy ->' prefix, no '(end of prompt)' closer, no blockquote/backtick-path wrapping.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Chain by back-reference + deterministic path, never invented alias.
rules_evaluated.evidence: P2 chains on P1's output via a scrollback-review back-reference ('the gap list I just ranked, the un-packaged-vs-packaged contrast moments, the dominant gap.') -- the preferred scrollback-review form named by the rule, not a file path (P1 produced no file, only chat analysis), so no deterministic-path or alias-drift risk applies.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Chained-prompt isolation — don't leak downstream pipeline.
rules_evaluated.evidence: P1's fence never mentions the coming rule-cut step; it stays self-contained to the diagnostic-ranking task and ends on 'which gap matters most?' without pre-grilling or deferring to P2.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: No session-resets mid-phase.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No /clear or 'start a new session' is offered between P1 and P2; P2 explicitly depends on the same session's scrollback ('this session's scrollback: the gap list I just ranked'), and the body never breaks that continuity. The one 'new session' in the file (L5 widget) is the module's own opening, not a mid-phase reset between P1 and P2.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Markdown shout (`**bold**`, `*italic*`) inside fenced prompts = dead weight in Claude Code.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Read both registry fence bodies in full -- no ** or single-* emphasis markers inside either fence (backtick code-spans for task.md/plan.md/CLAUDE.local.md are the allowed exception, not markdown shout).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Tell me what you wrote, not show me what you'll write.

Show me the line you cut and, in two sentences, why the diagnosis killed it.' -- past-tense 'cut' before the report ask, not a pre-confirm 'show me before you cut'.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Don't restate session CWD inside prompt body.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Neither fence restates an absolute path or a cd command; both reference relative paths (task.md, plan.md, ./CLAUDE.local.md) trusting the session's working directory. The one place a path IS named explicitly (L7, the M5 worktree path in the session-setup widget) sits outside any prompt fence entirely, so this rule doesn't reach it -- and would be exempt anyway under the rule's own carve-out since naming the worktree IS the action there.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Strong-bold prompt label is exactly `**Prompt**` — custom labels break renderer.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Both labels are exactly '**Prompt**' with a parenthetical destination/context suffix, never a custom label like '**Prompt: X**'.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Normal work request before orchestration.
rules_evaluated.evidence: P1 opens as a direct, concrete request grounded in artefacts the student already has (task.md, plan.md) rather than an interview ('Ask me which files...'). The four-dimension structure is pedagogical content (the diff method being taught), not orchestration bloat.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Prompts live in registry; module/exercise/lecture files reference by marker.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Body uses {{prompt:spot-gaps-build-the-loop-1}} (L24) and {{prompt:spot-gaps-build-the-loop-2}} (L39) markers, not inline fences. Naming matches the <file-slug>-<n> convention for shared-library exercises exactly (file slug: spot-gaps-build-the-loop).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Module names in prompt prose are fine — they ground the session.
rules_evaluated.evidence: P1's fence names 'm4/' and 'm5/' branches and worktree state directly -- this is the rule's own worked example (session artefacts module-numbered by design), not a curriculum-coined event label with no in-session referent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Disambiguation, anchors, and decision logic that bind Claude live INSIDE prompt fence.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Read both fences in isolation, no body context: P1 self-defines where task.md/plan.md live and what m4/m5 branches are without relying on any body callout. P2 assumes a warm session holding the just-produced gap list, which is a valid assumption given no reset separates P1 from P2 (see §7).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Wide prompts split by logical move — paragraph breaks = cheapest scan-affordance.
rules_evaluated.evidence: P1 splits into five paragraph-scale moves (context-setting; read-instructions; the four-dimension bullet list; quote-requirement; ranking-close). rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Body lead-in mirrors prompt's opening phrasing.

P1's pairing is closer: lead-in opens 'read both sessions', and the fence's first imperative (after one line of necessary context-setting) is 'Read both.' -- same verb, same object, close enough to rhyme.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Open the P2 lead-in on the fence's actual first move, e.g. 'Ask Claude to read CLAUDE.local.md and the session so far, then cut the one rule the diagnosis killed.'

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Verify session boundary before deciding prompt's context-carrying.

P2 runs warm relative to P1 (no reset between them, §7), and its back-references ('the gap list I just ranked', 'the un-packaged-vs-packaged contrast moments', 'the dominant gap') point at content P1's own fence explicitly produced in-session (the four-dimension walk + the ranking close), not a curriculum-coined Phase-heading label absent from scrollback (§40b) -- 40a's concurrent-worktree corollary doesn't apply (this file opens one worktree, not parallel ones).

rules_evaluated.evidence: P2's 'say so and stop' sits only in the conditional null-case branch ('If every rule still holds under diagnosis, say so and stop.'), not tacked onto the end of the main write-then-report path -- in the branch where a rule IS cut, the sequence is find -> cut (write) -> report, with no STOP undermining the write.
